new_packages.label: הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה וַחֲסָדִים מִצַּד הָאָב

bechina_evidence.source_quote: כִּי הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַחֲסָדִים כַּנַּ"ל
bechina_evidence.note: Explicit bechina-equivalence: 'Torah revelation IS hasadim revelation' — same essential nature

bechina_evidence.source_quote: אֲנִי אוֹמַר לְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹחַאי אַבָּא, בְּחִינַת הַחֲסָדִים מִצַּד הָאָב, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה
bechina_evidence.note: Torah = bechina of Yochai-aba = bechina of hasadim from the father: all three are identified as the same reality

bechina_evidence.source_quote: אֲנִי אוֹמַר לְיוֹחַאי אַבָּא... בְּחִינַת הַחֲסָדִים מִצַּד הָאָב
bechina_evidence.note: Yochai-aba is a bechina of hasadim-from-the-father: the name symbolizes the concept

new_packages.reason: The source text in paragraphs 12-13 contains three concepts connected by explicit bechina language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַחֲסָדִים') that form an independent positive domain: the principle that revealing Torah = revealing hasadim from the paternal side, and that 'Yochai aba' is the symbolic name for this Torah-hasadim source. This is a thematic cluster independent of malkhut/gadlut (Package 2) and independent of the drawing of divinity into the mind (Package 3). It answers a distinct question: where does Torah come from? Answer: from the paternal hasadim, which is what Torah revelation essentially is. The three nodes share the essential nature of being 'the source and substance of Torah revelation as an act of lovingkindness.'
new_packages.independence_argument: This cluster is not reducible to Package 2 (malkhut/gadlut) or Package 3 (drawing divinity into mind). Package 2 describes the STATE produced by Torah. Package 3 describes the EFFECT of Torah on the mind of the listener. This new package describes the NATURE/SOURCE of Torah itself as an act of revealing hasadim. These are three different aspects of the Torah teaching: source (Pkg 4), effect on listener (Pkg 3), result for teacher (Pkg 2).

observations: Torah #60 (LM2) is a compact teaching with a tight argument connecting three phenomena: (1) war/bloodshed causes drought by diverting the earth's vapors from rain to bloodshed; (2) teaching Torah to unworthy students also causes drought by inverting Torah honor (כבוד) into desecration (חלוף הכבוד / מרקוליס); (3) the story of R' Shimon and R' Akiva illustrates how revealing Torah = revealing hasadim from the father, and how a student-teacher relationship can bring a teacher from smallness (katnut) to greatness (gadlut). The bechina subgraph is sparse (5 edges, 9 nodes), reflecting that most of this Torah's connections are eitza (causal) chains linking the phenomena rather than bechina identifications. The three raw bechina components in the dataset — plus the proposed new cluster from the source text — together cover the Torah's main conceptual moves: the anti-honor force (Package 1, evil), the state of spiritual greatness that enables Torah (Package 2, good), the drawing of divinity into the mind through Torah (Package 3, good), and the paternal hasadim as the substance of Torah revelation (Package 4, proposed, good). The good/evil mirror is clear: Package 1 (evil) mirrors the Torah-honor complex; the positive packages (2, 3, and proposed 4) have no direct evil counterpart named in the dataset, though the text alludes to one: teaching Torah to an unworthy student draws divinity into an unworthy mind, which is the evil mirror of Package 3.
